behaviour.print_says: dead (one struck the lantern and was killed)

station.print_says: Printed 'Teesmouth lighthouse', but in this scanned copy 'Teesmouth' is struck through by hand and 'Whitby' is written in the margin with a caret (a manuscript correction)

date_iso.print_says: Oct. 13th and 15th — two separate days (1879-10-13 and 1879-10-15), not a range that includes the 14th
'taken in October' is said of the Leman and Ower; the list then runs on '; at the Galloper ...; also at the North Foreland', so October may or may not carry over

behaviour.print_says: 'immolating itself against the lanterns ... were taken ...; also at the North Foreland' — the verb is 'taken' (caught), within a sentence about killing themselves against the lanterns; no explicit 'killed' for North Foreland

at_light.print_says: true — 'a particular facility for immolating itself against the lanterns', of which North Foreland is given as an instance

station.print_says: Rhinus of Islay (misprint for Rhinns of Islay)

species.print_says: Linnet, Linota cannabina (heading; the Linnets were mixed with Larks)
Larks and Chaffinches (in the Sky Lark account)

at_light.print_says: true: 'Starlings, Blackbirds, and Thrushes in the vicinity of light from 1 to 4 a.m.; six Starlings, four Thrushes, and one Blackbird killed'

weather.print_says: severe weather ('The burst of severe weather during the early days in December')

station.print_says: Dhuheartach, Skervuile, and Rhinns of Islay (Lamlash is not named for the Nov. 15th-18th rush)

count.print_says: 'great numbers of birds ... of various species, of which Blackbirds, Thrushes, and Mavises were recognised' — the number refers to all birds, not Blackbirds alone

at_light.print_says: true — 'Starlings, Blackbirds, and Thrushes in the vicinity of light from 1 to 4 a.m.; ... one Blackbird killed'

time.print_says: 'from 1 to 4 a.m.' is given for the birds in the vicinity of the light; no separate time for the killing

behaviour.print_says: struck ("one struck at 10 a.m."; not said to be killed)

species.print_says: Sky Lark (section heading 'Sky Lark, Alauda arvensis'; the Newarp sentence names no bird)

at_light.print_says: 'taken' follows directly on 'a particular facility for immolating itself against the lanterns', but the sentence itself doesn't name the lantern

date_iso.print_says: On the 2nd March ... (March, 1880 stated in the text)

at_light.print_says: 'ten Larks and nine Starlings struck' — the lantern is not named, though striking at a light station implies it

behaviour.print_says: 'in vicinity of light' (not explicitly flying round it); 'many struck and went overboard' follows

species.print_says: Woodcocks (heading on preceding page; 'Woodcocks' named in this paragraph)

at_light.print_says: 'single birds striking at North Ronaldshay' — the lantern is not named

behaviour.print_says: dead ('a Sparrowhawk was killed ... and one on Aug. 15th' — the 'one' continues 'was killed')

time.print_says: as a rule, very early in the morning (4.30 to 9.20 a.m.)

wind.print_says: in three out of four instances S.W. (once, July 3rd, W.N.W.)

station.print_says: not named for Nov. 25th; species heading says 'Appeared at North Ronaldshay and the Bell Rock'

species.print_says: Titmice (TITMICE heading; the Flycatchers are only the birds they were seen amongst)

weather.print_says: always in hazy or rainy weather, generally "haze and rain" together

station.print_says: Printed 'Teesmouth lighthouse', but on this copy 'Teesmouth' is struck through by hand and 'Whitby' written in the margin
